oneLine: Bitcoin fell 0.3% and Ethereum rose 0.02% on Friday as stronger-than-expected US jobs data (165,000 vs. 65,000 forecast) triggered rate-hike expectations and a tech-stock selloff, leading to $430+ million in crypto ETF outflows.
caveman: Friday was a mixed but worrying day in crypto. Bitcoin went down less than one percent while Ethereum barely moved. The big news was that the US government released employment numbers—companies hired 165,000 workers, way more than people expected (they thought 65,000). When lots of new jobs appear, the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates, which makes people sell their riskier investments like Bitcoin. At the same time, artificial-intelligence stocks dropped sharply, so investors sold crypto to get cash. Over half a billion dollars came out of Bitcoin and Ethereum funds. It was a worrying day.
priceVolumeSummary: Bitcoin closed around $75,810–$75,917 (down 0.3%) and Ethereum around $2,237–$2,241 (up 0.02%) across major venues. Binance led volume with $11.5B in Bitcoin and $6.8B in Ethereum.
positioningSummary: Funding rates ranged from 2.5% to 11% annualized (Binance highest at 9.1%), with Bitcoin open interest up 2% and Ethereum up 2.8% on Binance. Large traders stayed heavily long (top position ratio 2.18 for Bitcoin, 2.15 for Ethereum), but the taker buy/sell ratio of 0.97 for Bitcoin showed slightly more selling aggression. Market breadth was strong at 72.8% of altcoins trading up, though fear & greed plunged from neutral (50) to fear (28).
stocksSummary: Asian equities rallied: Korean semiconductor makers led (SK Hynix +4.4%, Samsung +5.2%), followed by Hong Kong leveraged plays (CSOP Samsung 2x +10.2%, CSOP SK Hynix 2x +8.1%). US tech surged after strong jobs data (QNTX +22.8%, OKLO +20.5%, RKLB +15.4%). Oil fell on demand concerns (WTI -1.3%, Brent -1.9%), while natural gas rose 4.6%.

topThree.headline: U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past 65,000 estimate
topThree.what: The US Labor Department released October employment data showing 165,000 jobs added and unemployment falling to 4.1%, significantly exceeding the 65,000 forecast. This stronger-than-expected result increases the likelihood of a December interest rate hike, putting downward pressure on risk assets including Bitcoin.

topThree.headline: Treasury cuts off MEXC Global over alleged $16 billion in transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia
topThree.what: The US Treasury's FinCEN ordered US financial institutions to stop processing transfers involving MEXC Global, citing $16 billion in transactions connected to sanctioned regimes. MEXC is one of the world's largest crypto exchanges by trading volume; the ban cuts it from US dollar infrastructure.

topThree.headline: Bitcoin ETFs see $430–540 million in net outflows as tech selloff spreads
topThree.what: US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs recorded net outflows of $430 million to $540 million on Thursday (November 5), with Fidelity and BlackRock leading the sell-off as technology stocks collapsed. The outflows continued into Friday amid fresh tech concerns.

Regulation and policy.headline: US Treasury walks back crypto surveillance 'travel rule' proposal
Regulation and policy.what: The Treasury Department withdrew a controversial regulatory proposal that would have expanded compliance requirements for cryptocurrency transactions. The reversal removes a potential compliance burden that industry groups had strongly opposed.

Regulation and policy.headline: Greece approves 10% tax on crypto gains and 15% levy on staking/DeFi income
Regulation and policy.what: Greece passed a new crypto tax framework with a 10% capital gains levy, 15% on staking and DeFi income, and an annual exemption threshold of €500. Annual gains below that threshold are tax-exempt, and investors have 12 months to declare past holdings without late penalties.

Regulation and policy.headline: Trump administration moves closer to allowing crypto in 401(k) retirement plans
Regulation and policy.what: A rule that would open 401(k) retirement accounts to alternative assets including cryptocurrencies has reached the White House for final review. The proposal would allow retirement savers to allocate a portion of their accounts to digital assets.

Regulation and policy.headline: Russia finalizes crypto trading rules ahead of November 17 rollout
Regulation and policy.what: Russia completed its regulatory framework for crypto trading, allowing retail investors to trade Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT through regulated intermediaries. Moscow Exchange is planning to launch native crypto trading in December.

Regulation and policy.headline: Nigeria sets new crypto licensing rules, bans algorithmic stablecoins
Regulation and policy.what: Nigeria's central bank banned algorithmic stablecoins and introduced reserve requirements for stablecoin issuers. The move expands regulatory oversight of crypto payment services in the country.

Institutional flows and ETFs.headline: Strive adds 15,124 Bitcoin in October, approaches top corporate treasury holders
Institutional flows and ETFs.what: Bitcoin treasury firm Strive bought 15,124 BTC in October for approximately $1.2 billion, bringing its total holdings to 43,124 BTC. The company reported $509 million in net income for Q3 2026.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Binance cuts off SignalPlus after hackers break in via fake Microsoft Teams invite
Exchange and platform changes.what: Binance revoked API keys for the trading platform SignalPlus after an unauthorized breach using a spoofed Microsoft Teams job interview. SignalPlus later reported losses under $82,000 and began reimbursement; Deribit also disabled connected keys.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Hypercall to launch first Anthropic-linked pre-IPO options market
Exchange and platform changes.what: Trading platform Hypercall is launching options trading on Anthropic's pre-IPO shares, with calls, puts, and complex strategies available in select non-US jurisdictions. Trading is expected to begin Monday.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Aave Labs acquires Avon team for fixed-rate lending expansion
Exchange and platform changes.what: Aave Labs acquired the team and technology of Avon, an onchain protocol offering fixed-rate and floating-rate lending. The deal supports Aave's expansion into fixed-rate products.

Exchange and platform changes.headline: Thailand moves to block Bitget as crypto exchange's local acquisition faces uncertainty
Exchange and platform changes.what: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint against Bitget's operator, alleging it ran an unlicensed crypto exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025. The action complicates Bitget's planned local acquisition.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Gnosis Pay data breach exposes card details and customer personal data
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Crypto debit card provider Gnosis Pay disclosed unauthorized access to its legacy debit card system on November 3, exposing customer card details and personal information. Customer crypto funds were not affected; the company's enterprise card platform was uncompromised.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Ethereum software bug triggers emergency fixes across major layer-2 networks
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: A critical Ethereum-related software vulnerability was identified, prompting emergency patches across multiple layer-2 scaling networks. Fixes have been published, though operator adoption and impact on cross-chain routes remain under monitoring.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Binance hackers swapped stolen tokens for $124 million in Bitcoin
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Forensics firm Elliptic reported that the $6.3 billion Binance hackers have swapped stolen tokens for approximately $124 million in Bitcoin. Of the $6.3 billion stolen, $2.85 billion remains frozen, and most crypto has not been cashed out.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: Anthropic IPO valuation could be cut in half to $1 trillion after AI stock rout
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: Investors told the Wall Street Journal they believe Anthropic's valuation target of $1.5 trillion is too high in the wake of recent AI stock selloffs. Prediction markets are betting on a December listing, but the final valuation remains uncertain.

Unconfirmed and watch items.headline: Bitcoin and USDT attract premiums in Paraguay amid banking crisis
Unconfirmed and watch items.what: Bitcoin and USDT traded at premiums in Paraguay's peer-to-peer markets as the country faced a banking collapse and currency instability. The turmoil coincided with a 10% surge in the US dollar against the local peso.

calendarNotes.event: Non-Farm Employment Change (Nov 6, 13:30 UTC): Actual 165,000 jobs added, beating forecast of 65,000 and previous month's 29,000.
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Stronger-than-expected job growth typically boosts rate-hike expectations, creating downward pressure on risk assets like Bitcoin and crypto broadly.

calendarNotes.event: Average Hourly Earnings month-on-month (Nov 6, 13:30 UTC): Forecast 0.3%, previous 0.1% — actual result not yet published in data.
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Faster wage growth can support rate-hike expectations, reinforcing hawkish policy bets and pressuring risk assets.

calendarNotes.event: US CPI Report (Nov 10, 13:30 UTC): Upcoming inflation data will be closely watched for Fed policy signals.
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: CPI misses or beats inflation targets directly affect Federal Reserve interest rate decisions and typically move Bitcoin and equities sharply.

glossary.definition: The difference between the futures price and the spot price. A positive basis (futures higher) signals long positioning; negative basis signals short positioning.
The percentage of assets in a market that are trading up on the day. High breadth (over 70%) indicates broad-based strength.
A sentiment indicator ranging from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed). Readings below 30 signal fear, above 70 signal greed.
A periodic payment between long and short traders on futures exchanges. Positive rates mean longs pay shorts; negative rates mean shorts pay longs. Higher rates indicate more leverage and risk.
The ratio of open long positions to open short positions. A ratio above 1 means more traders are betting on price increases; below 1 means more are betting on decreases.
The reference price used to calculate funding payments and mark unrealized gains/losses on futures. It smooths out spot price swings to prevent manipulation.
The total value of all open futures contracts at an exchange. Rising OI often indicates new money entering the market; falling OI suggests positions are closing.
The day-to-day change in total open contracts. Positive change means new long or short contracts are opening; negative change means positions are closing.
The ratio of buy-side aggressive orders (takers) to sell-side aggressive orders. Above 1 signals more aggressive buying; below 1 signals more aggressive selling.
The long-to-short ratio among the largest traders at an exchange. A high ratio (e.g., 2.0) means the biggest accounts are heavily net long.
